script.title: The First Aircraft to Fly on Another World
script.description: On 19 April 2021, NASA's Ingenuity helicopter made history by performing the first powered flight on Mars. Captured by the Perseverance rover, the tiny craft survived years on the Red Planet.

shots.narration: On 19 April 2021, Ingenuity made the first powered, controlled flight on another planet.
The initial test was a three-metre hover lasting about 39 seconds above the Martian surface.
Flight is difficult because Mars air is about one percent as dense as Earth's at sea level.
To generate enough lift, the dual rotors must spin at around 2,400 revolutions per minute.
The small aircraft weighs 1.8 kg and relies on rotors spanning 1.2 metres to fly.
Engineers originally built the helicopter for just five test flights over 30 days.
Instead, it completed 72 flights over almost three years, reaching speeds up to 36 km/h.
Across those missions, it covered more than 17 kilometres and climbed as high as 24 metres.
The historic mission ended in January 2024 when a rotor blade was damaged on landing.
